title: inquiry.submitted v1.4 (TripPlanner → AA-Booking)
description: One row of tripplanner.outbox / tripplanner.v_inquiry_outbox (payload column). Written in the same transaction as the 'sent' trip event (ADR 0001 decision 6, AA-676). The consumer stores idempotency_key in its own inbox and processes each key once. Producer: AA-TripPlanner-Web backend/assembly/handoff.py. v1.4 (AA-908, root ADR 0006 Phase 4): additive over v1.3 — customer.identity carries the verified identity (iss, sub) of a traveller signed in with the Cognito EXTERNAL pool (pii:online_id, keyed on iss AND sub, never sub alone, ADR 0006 decision 9), or null for a guest. A signed-in send takes customer.email from the verified access token and sets verified to the token's email_verified; verified is true only together with an identity. A guest send is unchanged (verified false, identity null): a typed contact proves nothing. The token itself never crosses. AA-Booking links a verified identity to one customer (booking.customer_identities, bk-024) and never merges an unverified lead automatically. AA-Booking must accept 1.4 before TripPlanner sends it (consumer first, contracts rule 2). v1.3 (AA-986 L6, root ADR 0015 decision 5): additive over v1.2 — every leg and every day also says whether AA still serves its tour: `available`, `reason`, `reason_detail`. Stops whose tour AA no longer serves (retired, paused, or a stop the tour no longer has) are still handed off, after the served days and legs, with available false, so staff see why such a leg cannot be matched; the hand-off is never refused over it. v1.2 (AA-830): every leg carries the catalog tour key (source_system, source_id). Consumers must accept version 1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3 and 1.4 and key legs on (source_system, source_id), never on source_tour_id (data standards DM-2.2).

version.description: major.minor; 1.4 is additive over 1.3 (and 1.2, 1.1, 1); payloads labelled 1, 1.1, 1.2 or 1.3 are validated by those files

idempotency_key.description: <trip_id>:<handoff_id>. A re-send after a real edit is a new hand-off with a new key.

handoff_id.description: id of the 'sent' event in tripplanner.trip_events

customer.description: Who sent the inquiry. null = legacy guest hand-off (deprecated by O6: guests must give name + email). customer_id null = contact matched nobody verifiable or matched an existing customer without proof (TripPlanner never links on an unverified match); the fields then carry exactly what this request submitted.

customer_id.description: tripplanner.customers.id when this request created/claimed the customer; null for a contact snapshot

email.description: lower(trim()); required non-null by O6 once the TripPlanner guest form ships

consent.description: explicit contact consent from the registration form

verified.description: true only for a signed-in traveller whose token says email_verified (then identity is set and email is the token's address). A guest contact is always false. Consumers must not merge an unverified customer into an existing booking.customers row automatically.

identity.description: v1.4: the traveller's verified sign-in identity, read by TripPlanner from a validated EXTERNAL-pool access token at send time; null for a guest send. Key on (iss, sub) together. Personal data class online_id (DM-6.1).

iss.description: Token issuer as published by the pool (never hand-built).

legs.description: Consecutive days taken from the same real AA tour (ADR 0001 decision 5). day_from/day_to are that tour's own day indexes. Key a leg on (source_system, source_id). v1.3: legs of stops AA no longer serves come after the served legs (available false); their source_system / source_id name the catalog key when the producer knows it (the tour is in the tombstone or still served), else null.

source_tour_id.description: Kept for compatibility with v1 / v1.1 readers: the TripPlanner component's tour key as before, which is either a catalog source_id or a version tour_id (it changes on re-upload). Do not key on it; use source_system + source_id.

source_system.description: Catalog key system (catalog.v_tour.source_system). null together with source_id when the producer could not resolve source_tour_id against catalog.v_tour at send time (the tour left the catalog, or the catalog was unreadable); the hand-off is still sent.

source_id.description: Stable catalog tour key (catalog.v_tour.source_id = COALESCE(raw_tours.source_group_id, tour_id)); does not change on re-upload. null exactly when source_system is null.

available.description: true when AA serves the tour of this leg / day at send time (catalog.v_tour). false = the stop's tour left the catalog or no longer has this stop; see reason.

reason.description: null exactly when available is true. retired: AA no longer offers the tour (catalog.v_tour_retired state retired: deleted at the source, Master trashed, orphan supersede); paused: temporarily unavailable (any other tombstone state: Master inactive, or a supersede waiting for the new version's Master); stop_removed: the tour is still served but no longer has this stop; not_served: not in the catalog and no tombstone row (or the tombstone could not be read).

reason_detail.description: The CIS lifecycle reason from catalog.v_tour_retired.reason (e.g. source_deleted, master_trashed, superseded_orphan, master_inactive, superseded_pending) when reason is retired or paused; else null. Informational: consumers must not branch on values they do not know.

days.description: One entry per pinned component: the served ones in trip-day order (several components can share a day), then (v1.3) the ones whose tour AA no longer serves, with available false and their last known trip day (or the day after the last served day).

available.description: true when AA serves the tour of this leg / day at send time (catalog.v_tour). false = the stop's tour left the catalog or no longer has this stop; see reason.

reason.description: null exactly when available is true. retired: AA no longer offers the tour (catalog.v_tour_retired state retired: deleted at the source, Master trashed, orphan supersede); paused: temporarily unavailable (any other tombstone state: Master inactive, or a supersede waiting for the new version's Master); stop_removed: the tour is still served but no longer has this stop; not_served: not in the catalog and no tombstone row (or the tombstone could not be read).

reason_detail.description: The CIS lifecycle reason from catalog.v_tour_retired.reason (e.g. source_deleted, master_trashed, superseded_orphan, master_inactive, superseded_pending) when reason is retired or paused; else null. Informational: consumers must not branch on values they do not know.

custom_days.description: Days the traveller added on top of the AA legs (not part of any tour).
